findings.description: _read_all returns {} on OSError, ValueError or KeyError. A corrupt or transiently unreadable file looks like an empty store. The next save/delete/take_by_refresh then writes back only the new record, wiping every other live session. Also, TypeError/AttributeError from malformed items are not caught. Separately, sign_out_everywhere reads an empty list on a read failure and reports 0 revoked while sessions remain, so a password change would silently leave sessions alive.
findings.suggestion: Return {} only for FileNotFoundError. Raise StoreError for other read or parse failures so callers and writers do not overwrite or ignore the existing data.
findings.title: Read errors treated as an empty store, causing silent session loss

findings.description: FileSessionStore.get and all call _read_all without taking self._lock, while writers rewrite the file under the lock. os.replace is atomic so reads usually see a whole file. But the shared '.tmp' file and the read-modify-write sequences are only protected among writers in one process. Readers can return stale data to sign_out_everywhere, which then misses a session saved concurrently, e.g. a login racing a password change.
findings.suggestion: Take the lock in get and all, or document and handle the stale snapshot in callers.
findings.title: File store get/all read without the lock

findings.description: refresh() removes the old session via take_by_refresh before checking the user is active. If _issue then fails with a StoreError, the old session is already destroyed and no new one exists, so the user is logged out. This is a partial failure that leaves bad state.
findings.suggestion: Handle the failure of the issue step, e.g. by restoring the taken record on error, or by issuing the new session before deleting the old one within one atomic store operation.
findings.title: Refresh token consumed before validity checks, and new session issue can fail after consumption

findings.description: Unlike sign_out_everywhere, purge_expired does not catch StoreError around delete. One failed delete raises out of the loop, leaving the remaining expired sessions unpurged and losing the count. The returned count also claims all were deleted.
findings.suggestion: Catch StoreError per record, log it, and count only successful deletions.
findings.title: purge_expired aborts on the first store error

findings.description: sign_out_everywhere takes a snapshot of all records and deletes by access hash. A refresh in flight can take_by_refresh a record (removing it from the store, so the snapshot delete is a no-op) and then _issue a new session after the password change. The refresh only checked active, not that the password changed. The attacker's refresh token therefore survives a password change.
findings.suggestion: Add a store-level delete_by_user operation that is atomic, and invalidate refresh in-flight, e.g. via a per-user session generation checked in _issue.
findings.title: sign_out_everywhere can miss concurrently created sessions and leaves refresh race
